title: Your first three mocks: where the marks are going
summary: Across **3 full-length mocks** (MHT-CET 2025 and two BITSAT papers) your **Mathematics is your strongest subject** (32/40 on both BITSAT papers) and your Physics fundamentals are solid. Most of your lost marks come from three places: **organic chemistry**, the **electromagnetic induction / AC** chapter in Physics, and **guessing under negative marking** in BITSAT. Fixing the first and the last alone is worth roughly **40–60 marks** on a BITSAT paper.

weakTopics.subject: Chemistry
weakTopics.topic: Organic chemistry (reaction mechanisms, carbonyls, haloalkanes, biomolecules)
weakTopics.evidence: 7 correct out of 34 organic questions (21%) versus 55% on the rest of Chemistry; 8 organic questions skipped. Weakest: Biomolecules 0/4, Reaction Intermediates 0/3, Aldehydes & Ketones 1/4, Carboxylic Acids 1/4, Haloalkanes 1/3.
weakTopics.advice: This is a **concepts** gap, not carelessness: your wrong organic answers were spread across options rather than near-misses. Rebuild from carbocation/carbanion stability (inductive, resonance, hyperconjugation) → nucleophilic addition to C=O → named reactions (aldol, Cannizzaro, HVZ, Hofmann). Learn each named reaction as reagent → product → why. Biomolecules and polymers are short NCERT chapters — 2 evenings each, high return.

weakTopics.subject: Physics
weakTopics.evidence: 0 correct out of 9 questions across the three papers (2 skipped). Every other Physics chapter together: 61/101.
weakTopics.advice: One chapter, completely missing — so it's likely a single shaky foundation. Start with flux $\Phi = BA\cos\theta$ and Faraday/Lenz signs, then self-inductance $L = \mu_0 N^2A/l$ (note $L \propto N^2$), then AC: reactances $X_L = \omega L$, $X_C = 1/\omega C$, impedance and power factor. Do 25 mixed numericals from this chapter before the next mock.

weakTopics.subject: Logical Reasoning
weakTopics.topic: Visual puzzles (paper folding, dice, figure formation)
weakTopics.evidence: 1 correct out of 7, and 5 of the 7 were skipped. Non-visual LR (series, coding, directions, blood relations): 24/33.
weakTopics.advice: These are fast marks once you have a method. Paper folding: unfold **one fold at a time**, mirroring each hole across the fold line; a cut **on** a fold becomes one hole straddling it. Dice: find a face common to two views and rotate around it. 15 minutes a day for a week is usually enough.

weakTopics.subject: Chemistry
weakTopics.evidence: Kinetics 1/4 (2 skipped), Thermodynamics 1/4. Small samples — watch these in the next two mocks before investing heavily.
weakTopics.advice: Revise first-order integrated rate law and half-life tricks ($t_{1/2} = 0.693/k$; '1/4 left' = 2 half-lives), and $\Delta G = \Delta H - T\Delta S$ sign reasoning.

habits.title: Guessing is costing you about 23 marks per BITSAT paper
habits.detail: In the two BITSAT mocks you answered 69 questions wrongly, each costing −1. **39 of your 110 wrong answers overall were given in under 40 seconds** — much faster than your average of ~80 s on questions you got right. Rule for BITSAT: if you can't eliminate at least **two** options, leave it. In Chemistry BITSAT 2 you scored 11 right / 15 wrong — net only 18 marks from 26 answered questions.

habits.title: Too many easy questions lost
habits.detail: 57 questions tagged easy were answered wrongly across the three tests. Re-read the question stem before marking (units, 'not', 'maximum vs minimum'), and use the Mark for review flag on anything you answered in under 30 s.

habits.title: Use your Maths strength for time
habits.detail: Maths is reliable (~80%). In BITSAT, attempt Maths **first or second** while fresh, bank those marks quickly, and leave the remaining time for Chemistry where careful elimination matters most.
